sara_support: FYI escalated ticket from ACME (internal #4532). Customer reports that after today's model rollout (redwood/model-alpha-2.3.0) their long instruction prompts are being ignored partway through — behavior looks like truncation or lost instructions for requests > ~3k tokens. They say it used to work on v2.2.x.

sara_support: Example from customer: they send a single prompt with a long system/instruction block (~3500 tokens) followed by short user messages. Response dropps later constraints and starts hallucinating.

sara_support: Repro payload they shared (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/model-alpha-2.3.0",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"INSTRUCTIONS: <~3500 tokens of explicit persona, do X,Y,Z ...>"},
    {"role":"user","content":"Please follow the above and summarize last quarter."}
  ],
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "stream": false
}
```

sara_support: Response snippet they attached: starts OK for first few lines, then after a paragraph it ignores the persona and starts generic summaries. They say it used to follow persona for entire response on v2.2.1.

jia_support: Do we have the customer's request_id or full API response with request/response headers? need the request_id to pull runtime logs.

sara_support: Sent request_id in ticket: req_20260315_acme_72. Customer time 2026-03-15T09:28:11Z. They also sent a short test case we can run.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout of redwood/model-alpha-2.3.0 -> production started at 2026-03-15T09:12:02Z (10% traffic). Canary increase to 50% at 09:20:00Z. Full rollout completed at 09:25:48Z.

tom_engineering: Thanks. First guesses: 1) kernel/compilation path changed and maybe KV cache or prefix handling got a regression for long sequences. 2) quantization/kernel rounding differences changing tokenization alignments. 3) batching/prefix drop due to new batching window change — we've seen prefix eviction when continuous batching merges segments.

tom_engineering: Can you attach the exact failing request tokens (token ids) or at least token counts? also need shard/runtime logs for req_20260315_acme_72 (gathered via obs-guides).

sara_support: Pasted token counts from customer: input_tokens: 3614, prompt_tokens: 3614, they set max_tokens low (1024) as above. They attached the model response but not token ids.

evan_ml: Quick note: we had a change in the attention kernel selector for 2.3.0 that prefers optimized fused-attn for seq_len <= 2048 with fallback to nvllama path for longer contexts. If the selector misclassifies the effective seq_len (off-by-one or tokenization mismatch), we could end up with an incorrect KV cache layout and later tokens read garbage.

evan_ml: Also check for tokenizer changes in the new model artifact. We had a small change to prefix normalization that could shift token boundaries for large system prompts. That would change token counts but shouldn't cause 'forgetting' unless the runtime mishandles KV offsets.

jia_support: repro steps request from eng: can we run the customer's sanitized prompt against v2.2.1 and v2.3.0 in our staging infra (same hardware) and capture raw token stream + kv-checksum? If we can reproduce we can roll back.

tom_engineering: I'll try to repro on a pinned node. Need the exact binary/hash used in production for 2.3.0 and the model artifact key. Also check autoscaler logs around 09:25 — if a node from older kernel was mixed with new kernel, streaming/batching could have interleaved prefixes incorrectly.

sara_support: Attaching customer sanitized test case in the ticket. They've asked for an immediate mitigation — they want a rollback if this is a regression (impacting a handful of enterprise customers).

deploy-bot: Rollout note: automatic safety rollback not triggered. Manual rollback is allowed by SRE.

evan_ml: Proposed quick triage: 1) run customer's test on v2.2.1 and v2.3.0 on same hardware/driver. 2) check tokenization diff (tooling: tools/token-diff) 3) pull runtime kv-checksum logs for req_20260315_acme_72 4) check if any model variant fallback happened (e.g., 2.3.0 -> 2.3.0-quantized-compat).

tom_engineering: I'll run 1 & 3 now. If we can reproduce, recommend immediate rollback to v2.2.1 and open a priority bug.

sara_support: Customer asked for ETA. told them we'll investigate and either patch or rollback within 4 hours. They said they can tolerate a rollback.

tom_engineering: Update: I ran the sanitized test on v2.2.1 and v2.3.0 on the same g5 nodes. v2.2.1 follows the persona across entire output. v2.3.0 starts to diverge around token ~2600 — matches customer's report. I captured core logs and kv-checksum mismatch for v2.3.0 but not for v2.2.1.

tom_engineering: Error snippet from runtime log for v2.3.0:
```
[2026-03-15T09:30:12Z] runtime: kv_cache_validate failed: expected checksum 0x1a2b3c4d got 0xdeadbeef (segment 4)
[2026-03-15T09:30:12Z] runtime: falling back to truncated_kv_path
```

evan_ml: That kv checksum mismatch is exactly what I'd expect if the attention kernel reordered or mis-sized KV segments. Likely root cause in kernel selector or new packing logic in 2.3.0.

tom_engineering: Given clear repro and miscompare, I'm going to recommend immediate rollback to 2.2.1 for production and hold further rollout. I'll coordinate with SRE.

sara_support: I'll tell the customer we're planning a rollback and will run their test again post-rollback.

deploy-bot: Manual rollback to redwood/model-alpha-2.2.1 initiated by tom_engineering at 2026-03-15T09:45:02Z.

tom_engineering: Rollback completed at 2026-03-15T09:56:08Z. I'm re-running the customer's sanitized test against 2.2.1 in prod; initial run looks good — follows persona end-to-end.

sara_support: Customer updated ticket: "Thanks, after rollback things look normal again. We'll monitor and report if we see anything else." :relieved:

evan_ml: Next steps: create a failing unit/integration test using the customer's prompt (add to long-context regression suite), bisect the kernel/compile changes in 2.3.0, and block 2.3.0 until we have a patch. I'll open a PR to add token-level kv-checksum assertions to our CI for long sequences.

tom_engineering: Filed ENG-1457 with logs and bisect plan. Assigning to evan_ml and low-level kernels team.

sara_support: Closing loop with customer. I'll update the ticket and add a postmortem link once ENG-1457 lands.

jia_support: Thanks everyone. Good catch.

sara_support: (closing comment) we'll schedule a brief sync with product and SRE to review release gating for long-context changes.
